title: Mystery number machines
goal: I can find a mystery number by working backwards. I undo the last step first. I can use bars for before-and-after stories.

learn.intro: A number machine changes a number, one step at a time. To find what went IN, work backwards. Undo the LAST step first. Use the opposite: + and - undo each other, and so do × and ÷.

example.problem: Ali picks a secret number. He multiplies it by 3, then adds 5. He gets 29. What is his number?
steps: Undo the last step. It was + 5, so take away 5: 29 - 5 = 24.
Undo the first step. It was × 3, so divide by 3: 24 ÷ 3 = 8.

howto.title: How to work backwards
steps: Start at the OUT. Undo the last step first.

try.text: Mei picks a secret number. She multiplies it by 5, then takes away 8. She gets 32. What is her number? {b}

items.text: What is my number? Write it in the box.
Circle the step that undoes the first one.
items.explanation: The opposite of adding is taking away, and the opposite of multiplying is dividing. (a) - 7. (b) ÷ 5. (c) + 12. (d) × 3.

items.text: Find the number that went IN. Undo the last step first.
Fill in the missing number.
items.explanation: Undo the last step first. (a) 15 - 7 = 8, then 8 × 2 = 16. (b) 19 + 5 = 24, then 24 ÷ 4 = 6. (c) 78 - 8 = 70, then 70 ÷ 10 = 7.

items.text: This machine does × 4, then - 1. Fill in the table.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the 4 missing numbers. Do the OUT of IN 3 and 6 first, then work backwards for 31 and 39.

answer.text: 11 and 23 in the OUT row, 8 and 10 in the IN row

items.text: A fair machine gives stickers for tokens. Each token gives the same number of stickers, plus a bonus. 3 tokens give 11 stickers. 6 tokens give 17.
items.explanation: Try 2 stickers a token: 3 tokens give 6, and 11 - 6 = 5 is the bonus. Test 6 tokens: 12 + 5 = 17. It fits. 3 and 4 a token do not fit both. 10 tokens: 20 + 5 = 25.

items.text: Ali had some marbles. He lost 18 in a game. Then he won 25 marbles. Now he has 60.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Before he won 25, Ali had {b} marbles.

items.explanation: Undo the last step: 60 - 25 = 35. Undo the first step: 35 + 18 = 53. Check: 53 - 18 = 35, then 35 + 25 = 60.

items.text: Kumar puts his stickers into 4 boxes. Every box has the same number. He takes 3 stickers out of box 4. Now box 4 has 7 stickers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Each box had {b} stickers at first.

items.explanation: Box 4 had 7 + 3 = 10 stickers before he took 3 out. Every box had the same, so each box had 10. 4 boxes: 4 × 10 = 40 stickers.

items.text: Mei had some stickers. She bought 12 more. Then she put them equally into 4 albums, 5 in each album.

parts.label: a
parts.text: After buying 12 more, Mei had {b} stickers.

items.explanation: 4 albums with 5 stickers each: 4 × 5 = 20 stickers. That is after buying 12 more, so at first she had 20 - 12 = 8. Check: 8 + 12 = 20 and 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

items.text: Lily had some money. She bought a pen for $3 and a book for $8. She has $12 left.
Mei, Lily and Aisha have 51 beads altogether. Lily has 6 more than Mei. Aisha has 9 more than Mei.
items.explanation: Take away the extra 6 and 9: 51 - 6 - 9 = 36. Now 3 equal bars share 36, so each is 36 ÷ 3 = 12. Mei has 12, Lily 12 + 6 = 18 and Aisha 12 + 9 = 21. Check: 12 + 18 + 21 = 51.
items.hint: Take off the extra bits. Then share the rest equally.

items.text: Aisha had some stickers. She used 8 on a card. Then she got as many stickers as she had left. Now she has 30.

parts.label: a
parts.text: After the card, Aisha had {b} stickers.

items.explanation: Now she has twice the number she had after the card, so 30 is 2 equal parts: 30 ÷ 2 = 15. After the card she had 15. At first she had 15 + 8 = 23. Check: 23 - 8 = 15, then 15 + 15 = 30.
items.hint: Now she has 2 equal parts. Find one part first.

items.text: A machine does × 4, then + 1. Could it give this OUT? Try IN 1, 2, 3 ... first.
items.explanation: IN 1, 2, 3, 4 give 5, 9, 13, 17: always 1 more than the 4 times table. 29 = 28 + 1: yes. 30 is skipped (29, 33): no. 33 = 32 + 1: yes. 42 is skipped (41, 45): no.
items.hint: Write the first OUT numbers. What do you see?

items.text: A letter can stand for a mystery number. Let n be the mystery number. 3 × n + 4 = 25 means: 3 times the number, plus 4, makes 25.
items.hint: Work backwards, just like a machine.

items.text: Three jars have 36 beans altogether. 4 beans move from jar A to jar B. Then 6 beans move from jar B to jar C. Now every jar has the same number.

parts.label: b
parts.text: At first: jar A {b}, jar B {b}, jar C {b}

items.explanation: (a) 36 ÷ 3 = 12. (b) Undo B to C: jar C had 12 - 6 = 6 and jar B had 12 + 6 = 18. Undo A to B: jar B had 18 - 4 = 14 and jar A had 12 + 4 = 16. Check: 16 + 14 + 6 = 36.
items.hint: Undo the last move first. Jar C gave nothing, it got 6.

items.text: Make your own riddle. "I think of a number. I ... then I ... I get ..." The mystery number must be 12. Many answers work.

answer.text: Open. Example: I think of a number. I add 7, then multiply by 2. I get 38. (38 ÷ 2 = 19, 19 - 7 = 12.)

items.explanation: Start at 12 and go forwards: 12 + 7 = 19, 19 × 2 = 38. The riddle ends at 38. To solve it, work backwards from 38.

items.text: Machine A does × 2, then + 3. Machine B does - 5, then × 3. The OUT of A goes into B. The final OUT is 36.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The OUT of machine A was {b}

parts.label: b
parts.text: The number that went into A was {b}

items.explanation: Undo B: 36 ÷ 3 = 12, then 12 + 5 = 17. That is the OUT of A. Undo A: 17 - 3 = 14, then 14 ÷ 2 = 7. Check: 7 → 14 → 17 → 12 → 36.
items.hint: Undo machine B first. Then undo machine A.

items.text: I multiply a number by 4, then add 6. I get 38. My number: {b}
Kumar gave away 14 stickers, then bought 9. Now 31. At first: {b}
items.explanation: Undo buying 9: 31 - 9 = 22. Undo giving away 14: 22 + 14 = 36. Check: 36 - 14 = 22, 22 + 9 = 31.

items.text: Kumar doubles his number, then adds 9. He gets 25. His number: {b}
5 equal bags. Bag 5 has 4 left after losing 6. Pens in all: {b}
items.explanation: Bag 5 had 4 + 6 = 10 pens before. Every bag had 10, so 5 × 10 = 50 pens.
